claim.quote: provides the first electroweak observation of the neutron skin which is expected in a heavy, neutron-rich nucleus

key_value_text.quote: The result A_PV = 0.656 \pm 0.060 (stat) \pm 0.014 (syst) ppm corresponds to a difference between the radii of the neutron and proton distributions Rn - Rp = 0.33 +0.16 -0.18 fm and provides the first electroweak observation of the neutron skin which is expected in a heavy, neutron-rich nucleus.

name: PREX-I: measurement of the neutron radius of 208Pb

summary.plain: PREX's first run measured how electrons of opposite spin scatter from lead-208. The tiny difference gave a neutron radius larger than the proton radius: the first electroweak observation of a neutron skin, though with large uncertainty.
summary.technical: First measurement of the parity-violating asymmetry A_PV = 0.656 ± 0.060 (stat) ± 0.014 (syst) ppm in elastic scattering of polarised electrons from 208Pb, corresponding to R_n - R_p = 0.33 +0.16 -0.18 fm: the first electroweak observation of the neutron skin.

title: Measurement of the Neutron Radius of 208Pb Through Parity-Violation in Electron Scattering
why_it_matters: The neutron skin of a heavy nucleus constrains the density dependence of the symmetry energy of nuclear matter and thus the structure of neutron stars.
